body:
`certifiedWidth` is computed from wave 1 ONLY (packages/merge-forecast/lib/forecast.mjs:135-136 — `const wave1 = waves[0] ?? []`), but the name and the `--width` failure message both read as a property of the whole schedule. For a foundation-first DAG — the shape ADLC.md D2 explicitly recommends, 'foundation built first and merged before the fan-out' — wave 1 holds ONE ticket, so the number is 1 no matter how wide the graph gets later, and `--width 4` fails with a message that does not say why.

DECIDED — do not revisit: this is a NAMING defect, not a behaviour defect. The wave-1 number is genuinely useful ('how wide can I dispatch right now'). Keep the gate exactly as it is; stop the name doing two jobs.

WHAT TO BUILD, in packages/merge-forecast only:

1. Rename the computed value to `firstWaveWidth` and emit it in the result.
2. Add `scheduleWidth`: the widest any SINGLE wave can safely go — `max` over every wave of the existing greedy computation. `computeCertifiedWidth(waveIds, pairResults, threshold)` (forecast.mjs:203) is already generic over a wave; nothing in it is wave-1 specific, so reuse it per wave rather than writing a second algorithm.
3. Keep `certifiedWidth` in the result as a DEPRECATED ALIAS equal to `firstWaveWidth`. Existing consumers read it (lib/output.mjs:70, bin/merge-forecast.mjs:109, the README, this package's own tests, and antigravity-booster's applyMergeForecast reads `recommendedWidth ?? certifiedWidth`). Removing it is a breaking change and is NOT in scope.
4. `recommendedWidth` keeps its current formula and meaning — `min(firstWaveWidth, backpressureWidth?, --width?)`. No behaviour change.
5. Make the gate message actionable: when `--width` exceeds the first-wave number, say that this gate checks WAVE 1 and report `scheduleWidth` alongside, so the operator learns why a foundation-first DAG fails and what the schedule could support. Exit code and pass/fail behaviour are UNCHANGED.
6. Update lib/output.mjs to print both numbers, plus the README and bin --help text.
7. The empty/early-return result shapes (forecast.mjs:47, bin/merge-forecast.mjs:109) must carry the new fields too, or a consumer sees `undefined` on the empty path.

RAILS: packages/merge-forecast/lib/signals.mjs and packages/merge-forecast/lib/reachability.mjs. Pair SCORING and WAVE computation must not change — only how width is reported. If either seems to need editing, stop and say so.

WRITE THE RED TESTS FIRST in packages/merge-forecast/test/forecast.test.mjs:
  - a foundation-first DAG (1 -> 4 parallel -> 1) reports `firstWaveWidth` 1 and `scheduleWidth` 4 — the motivating case, which is the whole point
  - `certifiedWidth === firstWaveWidth` on every result, so the alias cannot drift
  - a flat DAG with no edges reports firstWaveWidth === scheduleWidth
  - a wave whose tickets conflict pairwise lowers `scheduleWidth` below that wave's size
  - `--width` gate behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged: same exit code, same pass/fail boundary as before
  - the gate message names wave 1 and reports scheduleWidth
  - the empty-ticket path returns both new fields, not undefined

ACCEPTANCE
- Every red test fails before the change and passes after.
- `npm test` green from the repo root, output shown.
- `adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this ticket id>` exits 0, proving signals.mjs and reachability.mjs were untouched.
- `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs` exits 0 on the diff.
title: merge-forecast: name the wave-1 number honestly and add a schedule-wide width (#997)
